description:
You can explain yourself for twenty minutes and still leave a conversation feeling unheard. So what helps your words land—and what do you need to understand before you say them?

In this episode of I'll Just Let Myself In, Lish Speaks breaks down five pillars of communication: clarity, active listening, mutual understanding, relevance, and assertiveness. Drawing on her marriage, friendships, and family relationships, she gets honest about the work behind saying what you need and making room for someone else's truth.

The conversation moves from recognizing your own feelings to choosing the right moment for a difficult conversation. Lish also shares how prayer and her understanding of Pentecost connect to communicating across emotional differences. The goal is to speak with care, listen with humility, and recognize what is yours to change.

In this episode:
• Get clear about your feelings before asking someone else to understand them.
• Listen to understand instead of preparing your reply.
• Recognize when a conversation has stopped being mutual.
• Bring up the past with purpose and choose the right setting.
• Express your needs respectfully before silence becomes resentment.

Which of these five pillars is hardest for you right now? Share your thoughts in the comments, subscribe, and send this episode to someone you'd like to communicate with more honestly.

titles.reasoning: Names the practical framework; the overlay makes its personal purpose immediate.

titles.visual_direction: Lish mid-explanation with an open hand and an earnest expression, cropped on the right; large overlay in open space on the left.
titles.reasoning: Connects an everyday skill to the emotional cost of holding back.

titles.title: How to Listen Without Planning Your Reply
titles.visual_direction: A thoughtful close-up of Lish angled slightly toward the center; a single uncluttered speech shape opposite her with the overlay.
titles.reasoning: Offers one recognizable behavior to change, with a complementary action in the overlay.

titles.title: How to Bring Up the Past Without Losing the Conversation
titles.visual_direction: Lish with a measured, open-palmed gesture on the left; one simple looping arrow fades behind the overlay on the right.
titles.reasoning: Keeps the nuance that past experiences can be relevant when their purpose is clear.

titles.title: Faith and Communication: Finding the Words for Hard Talks
titles.visual_direction: Lish with a reflective expression, framed slightly off-center against a warm plain background; overlay beside her at eye level.
titles.reasoning: Makes the episode’s Christian perspective visible without promising a guaranteed outcome.

titles.title: You Said Everything. Why Do You Still Feel Unheard?
titles.visual_direction: Lish with a questioning expression on the right; two offset speech-bubble outlines on the left, with the overlay between them.
titles.reasoning: Starts with a familiar frustration and invites viewers into the communication framework.

titles.title: The Pause That Changed How Lish Listens
titles.visual_direction: Lish listening with an attentive expression, cropped close on the left; a small pause symbol under the overlay on the right.
titles.reasoning: Uses the specific friendship story to introduce active listening rather than vague transformation.

titles.title: What Are You Really Saying When You Say Nothing?
titles.visual_direction: Lish looking thoughtful with her hands gently clasped; generous blank space above her shoulder for the overlay.
titles.reasoning: Creates curiosity around withheld needs and the resentment discussed in the episode.

titles.title: The Conversation Before the Difficult Conversation
titles.visual_direction: Lish in a reflective three-quarter portrait beside a plain notebook; place the overlay across the empty opposite half.
titles.reasoning: Points to the private work of identifying feelings before trying to express them.

titles.title: What Lish Learned About Communication From Pentecost
titles.visual_direction: Lish with an engaged, thoughtful expression on the left; two simple speech shapes meeting on the right beneath the overlay.
titles.reasoning: Highlights a distinctive faith reflection and its connection to emotional understanding.

titles.title: Being Clear Doesn’t Mean They’ll Understand You
titles.visual_direction: Lish with a composed, firm expression centered slightly left; a fine vertical line separates her from the overlay on the right.
titles.reasoning: Preserves the limit Lish places on what clear communication can control.

titles.title: You Can Win the Argument and Miss the Person
titles.visual_direction: Lish speaking with a steady expression and one open hand; overlay on the opposite side, with no opponent or staged confrontation.
titles.reasoning: Frames the discussion’s emphasis on understanding rather than entering a conversation to be right.

titles.title: Keeping Quiet Isn’t Always Keeping the Peace
titles.visual_direction: Lish with a knowing, gently challenging expression on the right; the overlay sits alone in open space on the left.
titles.reasoning: Uses the episode’s challenge to avoidance while the word “always” preserves nuance.

titles.title: Honesty Doesn’t Have to Be Brutal
titles.visual_direction: Lish mid-conversation with a warm but serious expression; balanced close crop on the left and oversized overlay on the right.
titles.reasoning: Connects respectful assertiveness with the episode’s explicit caution about brutal honesty.

titles.title: Listening Doesn’t Mean You Have to Reconcile
titles.visual_direction: Lish with a grounded, reassuring expression, shoulders visible; overlay in the open upper-left area, with minimal visual decoration.
titles.reasoning: Names a specific boundary in the conversation without implying reconciliation is always wrong.
